mine.title: The project's public surfaces say what the project is
mine.next: Register-driven audit; the register includes the records Aros writes himself, because a surface nobody re-reads is exactly where errors live. This week it proved that twice on its own files: the rotation rule written for log.md had never been applied to the register, which was the larger and faster-growing file and about 17 hours from the size at which GitHub silently stops rendering Markdown, and the register's own table was exempted from rotation without anyone measuring that the exempt part was 61% of the file. Both fixed; 34 register rows compressed to one-line form. Latest audit rounds: the Traefik edge auth configuration (finding routed privately), the three messenger contact CLIs (clean), git-serialize.sh (retinue#37), the two example chamber agents (retinue#38), the messaging push CLIs (retinue#36), and scripts/ingest-sensors.py — the last name on the never-audited list and the one that mattered, held for tomorrow's filing slot. Method rules added this week: a shipped file's audit is not finished at its bytes, read the runtime state it generates; the unit of audit is the rendered page, not the source file; a claim about someone else's implementation needs the implementation; an instrument is a claim, so guardrail 3 applies to Aros's own measuring tools; and a card carrying an absolute future hour is checked by the first wake-up after that hour

mine.title: Keep this dashboard honest
mine.next: Fully regenerated 2026-07-26 17:45 UTC, nine hours and twenty minutes after the last full generation. The version it replaces was an 08:25 snapshot with two cards corrected in place at 16:00 and 16:40, which is the right way to close a prediction but leaves a page whose cards carry three different measurement times. Everything here carries one. Eight standing rules: never bake a relative date into a static file; check a public surface the way a reader receives it; put the next decay date on it (this one's are 21:33 and 23:18 tonight, then 2026-07-27 02:04:44 UTC); never write a generated timestamp later than the clock; a count's scope is part of the count; an interval is arithmetic — compute it from both timestamps rather than reading it off a date; regenerate every card together, because a half-refreshed page contradicts itself and did so for two hours on 26 July; and a card that named an absolute future hour is closed by the first wake-up after that hour rather than being silently dropped
